newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS OUTLOOK TIED TO U.S. FIGURES FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS OUTLOOK TIED TO U.S. FIGURES FRIDAY.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) traded in a narrow range on Thursday and were seen setting out quietly on Friday ahead of the release of U.S. jobs data.
"(The data) will set the next direction," one trader said.
A rise in German jobless gave a small early fillip to the market on Thursday, pushing yields slightly lower.

But around 1600 GMT the benchmark 10-year March 2007 OLO yield was unchanged on the day at 5.74 percent, after trading in a 5.73/76 range. The spread over German Bunds was one basis point narrower at six basis points.
March OLO future contracts were up 0.09 at 122.25.
One trader said an aggressive flattening move at the long-end of the Belgian OLO curve continued on Thursday.
"There's a big buyer in OLO 12s (8.00 pct, Dec 2012) and 23s (8.00 pct, March 2015)," he said.
Another trader said, however, buying was limited to the morning session and thin compared with earlier in the week.

OLO 12 was yielding 6.21 percent late on Thursday, compared with 6.22 at the start of trade and levels around 6.25 on Wednesday lunchtime. The yield on OLO 23 was 6.33 percent, down from 6.34 at Thursday's start and 6.36 at midday on Wednesday.
The rise in German jobless to 4.66 million, a new post-World War Two high, failed to support the short end of the yield curve, traders said.

Money market rates were steady. The franc however slipped again below 20.63 to the mark, after briefly trading above that level on Wednesday. The franc was quoted at 20.6320/30 in late trade, down from 20.6290/00 late on Wednesday.
